title.name: Title
title.value: A parent’s guide to Science and Technology, Grades 1–8 (2022)

content.name: Content
content.value: use a scientific research process, a scientific experimentation process, and an engineering design process to conduct investigations, following appropriate health and safety procedures

content.name: Content
content.value: use a scientific research process and associated skills to conduct investigations

content.name: Content
content.value: use a scientific experimentation process and associated skills to conduct investigations

content.name: Content
content.value: use an engineering design process and associated skills to design, build, and test devices, models, structures, and/or systems

content.name: Content
content.value: follow established health and safety procedures during science and technology investigations, including wearing appropriate protective equipment and clothing and safely using tools, instruments, and materials

content.name: Content
content.value: communicate their findings, using science and technology vocabulary and formats that are appropriate for specific audiences and purposes

content.name: Content
content.value: use coding in investigations and to model concepts, and assess the impact of coding and of emerging technologies on everyday life and in STEM-related fields

content.name: Content
content.value: write and execute code in investigations and when modelling concepts, with a focus on obtaining input in different ways for a variety of purposes

content.name: Content
content.value: identify and describe impacts of coding and of emerging technologies on everyday life, including skilled trades

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the practical applications of science and technology, and of contributions to science and technology from people with diverse lived experiences

content.name: Content
content.value: describe practical applications of science and technology concepts in various occupations, including skilled trades, and how these applications address real-world problems

content.name: Content
content.value: investigate how science and technology can be used with other subject areas to address real-world problems

content.name: Content
content.value: analyse contributions to science and technology from various communities

title.name: Title
title.value: Relating Science and Technology to Our Changing World

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the importance of biodiversity, and describe ways of protecting biodiversity

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the benefits of biodiversity and the consequences of the diminishing of biodiversity

content.name: Content
content.value: analyse a local issue related to biodiversity while considering different perspectives; plan a course of action in response to the issue; and act on their plan

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of biodiversity, its contributions to the stability of natural systems, and its benefits to humans

content.name: Content
content.value: describe the distinguishing characteristics of different groups of organisms, and use these characteristics to further classify these organisms using a classification system

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of biodiversity as the diversity of life on Earth, including the diversity of organisms within species, among species in a community, and among communities and the habitats that support them

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which biodiversity within species is essential for their survival

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which biodiversity within and among communities is essential for maintaining the resilience of these communities

content.name: Content
content.value: describe interrelationships within species, between species, and between species and their natural environment, and explain how these interrelationships sustain biodiversity

content.name: Content
content.value: explain how invasive species reduce biodiversity in local environments

content.name: Content
content.value: explain how climate change contributes to a loss of biodiversity, and describe the impact of this loss

content.name: Content
content.value: describe the importance of biodiversity in supporting agriculture, including Indigenous agriculture around the world

title.name: Title
title.value: Relating Science and Technology to Our Changing World

content.name: Content
content.value: evaluate the impact of the use and generation of electrical energy on society and the environment, and suggest ways to use electrical energy responsibly

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the short- and long-term impacts of electrical energy generation technologies in Canada on society and the environment, including impacts on First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, and on climate change

content.name: Content
content.value: assess choices that reduce personal use of electrical energy from both renewable and non-renewable sources, and advocate for the responsible use of electrical energy by the school community

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the principles of electrical energy and its transformation into and from other forms of energy

content.name: Content
content.value: explain commonly observed electrostatic phenomena, using the principles of static electricity

content.name: Content
content.value: describe current electricity, and compare and contrast current electricity with static electricity

content.name: Content
content.value: identify materials that are good conductors of electric current and materials that are good insulators

content.name: Content
content.value: describe how technologies transform various forms of energy into electrical energy

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which electrical energy is transformed into other forms of energy

title.name: Title
title.value: Relating Science and Technology to Our Changing World

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the environmental impacts of flying machines

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the impacts on society of aviation technologies, while considering both local and global perspectives

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the ways in which properties of air can be applied to the principles of flight and flying machines

content.name: Content
content.value: identify flight-related applications of the properties of air

content.name: Content
content.value: describe the relationships between the four forces of flight – lift, weight, thrust, and drag – that make flight possible

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which flying machines and various organisms use balanced and unbalanced forces to control their flight

content.name: Content
content.value: describe ways in which the four forces of flight can be altered

content.name: Content
content.value: describe characteristics and adaptations that enable organisms to fly

content.name: Content
content.value: explain the functions of the components of a simple electrical circuit

content.name: Content
content.value: distinguish between series and parallel circuits, and identify common uses of each type of circuit

title.name: Title
title.value: Relating Science and Technology to Our Changing World

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the impact of space exploration on humans, society, and the environment

content.name: Content
content.value: analyse the impact that conditions in space have on humans engaged in space exploration, and explain how humans meet their social, emotional, and physiological needs in space

content.name: Content
content.value: assess the role of space exploration technology in observing and understanding environmental changes on Earth, including climate change

content.name: Content
content.value: evaluate the social and environmental impacts of space exploration, while taking various perspectives into consideration

content.name: Content
content.value: demonstrate an understanding of the solar system, the phenomena that result from the movement of different bodies within it, and the technologies used in space exploration

content.name: Content
content.value: identify components of the solar system, including the Sun, Earth and other planets, natural satellites, comets, asteroids, and meteoroids, and describe their main physical characteristics

content.name: Content
content.value: distinguish between the concepts of mass and weight

content.name: Content
content.value: describe the relationship between the force of gravity and the weight of a body

content.name: Content
content.value: identify the types of bodies in space that emit light and those that reflect light

content.name: Content
content.value: describe various effects of the relative positions and motions of Earth, the Moon, and the Sun

content.name: Content
content.value: identify various technologies used in space exploration, and describe how technological innovations have contributed to our understanding of space
